name: Your Problem, the Blues
why_it_works: Everyone already sings about their problems in their head. Turning the customer's exact frustration into a slow blues makes them laugh and feel seen at once, and the blues shape (the problem, the problem again, then a worse twist) promises a resolution, which is where {{brand}} walks in.

hook.pattern: Sing the customer's everyday frustration in a dead-serious blues voice; the mismatch between drama and problem stops the scroll.
examples: A slow blues for anyone with {{pain_short}} trouble.
Every {{pain_short}} problem deserves a proper blues song.

variables.name: brand
variables.description: Business name as sung, 4 syllables or fewer (use a short form if needed)

variables.name: pain_short
variables.description: Two-to-four-syllable lowercase label for the problem, used in 'the ___ blues'

variables.name: pain_point
variables.description: The everyday problem in the customer's words, capitalized, one breath, 8 syllables or fewer

variables.name: pain_detail
variables.description: A specific, relatable detail that makes it worse and rhymes with the pain point, capitalized, 9 syllables or fewer
variables.example: Last shop shrugged and charged me for it

variables.name: pain_scene
variables.description: The problem as one picture with no faces
variables.example: a glowing orange check-engine light on a dark dashboard

variables.name: fix_line
variables.description: The plain promise of what the business does, lowercase, true and provable, 8 words or fewer
variables.example: we show you the problem before we fix it

variables.name: pro_tip
variables.description: One save-worthy, general tip from the business, capitalized, 25 words or fewer, not personal advice
variables.example: A flashing check-engine light means pull over soon. A steady one means book a check this week.

variables.name: offer
variables.description: Low-risk next step, capitalized, 6 words or fewer because it is spoken in 2 seconds

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 photo of a frustrated person slumped at a kitchen table at dawn, head in hands, cool blue light, moody and cinematic
Vertical slow zoom on {{pain_scene}}, shallow focus, blue tint, 9:16

beats.purpose: bar 2, line A repeated, sung harder

visual.prompt: Same person now dramatically singing to the ceiling, blues club spotlight gag in a plain kitchen, vertical

beats.purpose: bar 3, line B: the twist detail

visual.prompt: Vertical photo of an empty wallet held upside down, a single coin falling, warm desk lamp light

beats.purpose: bar 4, turnaround: the brand enters, chord goes major

visual.prompt: Client-supplied photo of the real {{brand}} team helping someone, bright daylight, brand colors

beats.purpose: ring-out: CTA over the held major chord (half a bar)

music.feel: slow 12/8 blues shuffle, slide guitar and harmonica, bright major final chord

slides.headline: The {{pain_short}} blues
slides.body: A four-bar blues about a problem you know. Swipe if you've lived it.
slides.visual_prompt: Moody title slide, old blues record label design with the title, deep blue tones

slides.headline: Bars 1 and 2
slides.body: {{pain_point}}. Sing it twice, the second time harder.
slides.visual_prompt: Person staring at the problem in blue morning light, vertical, film grain

slides.headline: Bar 3: it gets worse
slides.visual_prompt: Empty wallet or stack of confusing paperwork on a table, warm lamp

slides.headline: Before you pay anyone to fix it
slides.body: Ask three things: what is wrong, what it costs in writing, and what happens if you wait.
slides.visual_prompt: Clean checklist slide with three ticked boxes on a warm paper background, blue accent

slides.headline: One tip from {{brand}}
slides.visual_prompt: Simple tip card with a lightbulb icon, brand colors, plenty of space for text

slides.headline: Bar 4: the chord goes major
slides.visual_prompt: Bright warm client-supplied photo of the {{brand}} team at work, brand colors

slides.headline: End the song
slides.visual_prompt: Clean end card with {{brand}} logo and the offer, brand colors

craft.technique: Compressed 4-bar AAB blues with a major turnaround
craft.notes: The 12-bar AAB shape squeezed to one bar per line. At 60 BPM one bar of 4 is 4 seconds: a three-beat pickup (3s) carries the hook, bar 1 states the problem (A), bar 2 repeats it harder (A), bar 3 twists it with a worse detail that rhymes with A (B), bar 4 is the turnaround where the brand enters and the chord goes from dominant to bright major, then the CTA rides a half-bar ring-out (2s): 3 + 16 + 2 = 21 seconds. Stress the pain word on beat 1 of each bar and keep each sung line to one breath, about 8 syllables. Tempo/feel: 60 BPM slow 12/8 shuffle, slide guitar or harmonica, a quick drum fill into the major bar.

do_not: Mock the customer; laugh at the problem, not the person
Name or imply a specific real competitor as the 'last shop'
Promise a fix, outcome or price you can't guarantee
compliance: Law firms: no guarantees or implied outcomes ('we'll win your case'); include required attorney-advertising disclaimer and follow your state bar rules
Insurance and mortgage: no promised rates, approvals or savings amounts; include license number (NMLS for mortgage) and 'terms and eligibility apply'
Dental: do not guarantee pain-free or specific results; pain points must not reveal any real patient's information
The tip slide is general information, not legal, financial or medical advice, and says so where the niche requires it
Team photos are real staff, client-supplied, with consent; never a generated person shown as staff
